summary:
The DaVinci International Film Festival (DIFF) is an annual Los Angeles festival produced by the nonprofit DaVinci Film Society. Founded in 2017 by filmmaker Chadwick Pelletier, it recognizes independent films and screenplays through Official Selections and awards, including the Leo Award, its top honor. Programs include the Storyline screenwriting competition, ultra-short-film program GENiUS, documentary program DIFFdocs, and DaVinci Labs.

DIFF began screening films in 2018 and has since featured narrative, short, animated, documentary, and screenplay competitions, alongside industry panels and special events. Its 2020 and 2021 editions were held online during the COVID-19 pandemic; later festivals returned to in-person screenings at AMC Theatres at The Grove in Los Angeles. The 2024 edition introduced a Creativity Conference and Junior Leo Awards, and honored Michael J. Fox with the festival’s inaugural Visionary Award.

In 2025, DIFF launched FilmAfrica to promote African cinema, beginning with programming at its Los Angeles festival and plans for an independent awards platform in Nairobi in 2026, developed with the Swahili Village Group and Kenya Film Commission. That year, the festival also held its first DaVinci Masquerade at the Carlton Cannes Hotel during the Cannes Film Festival, with proceeds supporting the Society’s arts and sciences initiatives.

The festival’s 2025 and 2026 editions continued its expansion with new screenings, panels, and awards. The 2026 event included a *Braveheart* retrospective, a presentation to filmmaker Randall Wallace, and a new sports short-documentary award. DIFF is run by Pelletier and a nonprofit board, with an international presence and advisory representatives in France and Monaco. Its stated mission is to support independent creatives across the arts and sciences.
